1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, wherein the non-native compartment is formed by the assembly of a plurality of distinct BMC polypeptides.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme for a specific metabolic conversion.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides that are derived from various sources.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides characterized by distinct functional properties.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment, wherein the non-native compartment comprises a proteinaceous shell formed by the assembly of said at least one BMC polypeptide.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments formed through assembly of distinct types of proteinaceous shells.
